items.followUp: Write the balanced equations for the reactions of chlorine with cold, dilute sodium hydroxide and hot, concentrated sodium hydroxide.

rubric.why: The cold-condition equation must show the correct products and be balanced.
rubric.description: Balanced reaction of chlorine with cold sodium hydroxide.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the balanced equation producing sodium chloride and sodium hypochlorite.

rubric.why: The hot-condition equation must show the correct products and be balanced.
rubric.description: Balanced reaction of chlorine with hot sodium hydroxide.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the balanced equation producing sodium chloride and sodium chlorate.

modelAnswer: Cold, dilute conditions: Cl₂ + 2NaOH → NaCl + NaClO + H₂O

items.followUp: Define solubility and explain why sodium chloride dissolves in water.

rubric.why: Solubility states the maximum amount of solute that can dissolve.
rubric.description: Maximum amount of solute that dissolves.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that solubility is the maximum amount or quantity of solute that dissolves.

rubric.why: The definition must specify the solvent and the conditions for the saturated solution.
rubric.description: Amount is related to a given amount of solvent and formation of a saturated solution at a stated temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for including the solvent, saturated-solution condition, and temperature.

rubric.why: Sodium chloride is composed of sodium ions and chloride ions.
rubric.description: Identifies the ions in sodium chloride.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying both sodium and chloride ions.

rubric.why: Water molecules attract and surround the ions, enabling sodium chloride to dissolve.
rubric.description: Explains dissolution by attraction or hydration of the ions by water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that water attracts or surrounds the ions, or hydrates them.

modelAnswer: Solubility is the maximum amount of a solute that dissolves in a given amount of solvent to form a saturated solution at a specified temperature.
Sodium chloride consists of Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions.
Water is polar; its molecules attract and surround these ions, allowing sodium chloride to dissolve.
